hints: Look at what is attacking the carbonyl group, the electron-rich cyanide ion, and ask yourself if it is a nucleophile or an electrophile.
Count carbons carefully, ethanal already has 2 carbons and the CN group adds one more carbon to the chain.
Combine the addition type with IUPAC naming, the product has 3 carbons with both an OH and a CN group to name as a hydroxynitrile.
walkthrough:
**Identify the mechanism type**

Think like the carbonyl group. The C=O bond is polar, so the carbon is slightly positive and loves to be attacked by electron-rich species.

Here the attacker is $\text{CN}^-$, which has a lone pair and a negative charge. That makes it a nucleophile, so this is nucleophilic addition.

**Draw the addition product**

The $\text{CN}^-$ adds to the carbonyl carbon, then $\text{H}^+$ adds to the oxygen to give an alcohol.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CN}$$

**Name the cyanohydrin correctly**

Now count the longest chain including the nitrile carbon. We started with 2 carbons in ethanal, plus 1 new carbon from CN, so total is 3.

With 3 carbons, an OH on carbon 2, and a nitrile group, the name is 2-hydroxypropanenitrile. That gives nucleophilic addition plus 2-hydroxypropanenitrile.

options.A: Product name is correct but reaction type is wrong. $\text{CN}^-$ is a nucleophile donating an electron pair to the delta-positive carbonyl carbon, not an electrophile. Students often mix up the terms because addition to C=C is electrophilic, but addition to C=O is nucleophilic.
options.B: Both parts are wrong. It is not electrophilic addition, and 2-hydroxyethanenitrile would only have 2 carbons. This forgets that the carbon from HCN becomes part of the main chain, increasing ethanal (C2) to a C3 product.
options.C: This is correct on both counts. $\text{CN}^-$ acts as a nucleophile attacking ethanal in nucleophilic addition, and the product $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CN}$ contains 3 carbons, so it is named 2-hydroxypropanenitrile.
options.D: Reaction type is correct but product name is wrong. 2-hydroxyethanenitrile is the product from methanal ($\text{HCHO}$ + HCN), not ethanal. With ethanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$), you must add the extra CN carbon to get a 3-carbon propanenitrile.
